style: recurring orange-cream market clerk fox; editorial fable; no text

items.title: Create a Print.World collection for the first believers
items.description: Build a limited NFT collection that identifies people who joined the experiment early. Use Print.World and the available Binder/collection tooling. The collection should say “I was here when this was uncertain,” not “I am guaranteed tokens.” Define supply, eligibility, metadata, token-binding rules, transferability, and failure behavior before minting. A holder may later transfer or sell the NFT if a market exists; never describe that as guaranteed liquidity.

items.title: Name the cohort
items.description: Give the first-believer group a name that is larger than the current ticker and survives a price chart.

items.title: Write the collection constitution
items.description: State who can mint, how many exist, whether they can be transferred, what the creator may change, and what cannot be changed.

items.title: Make the collection useful if the token dies
items.description: The NFT should preserve a story, artwork, status, or access right even if the token reaches zero.

items.title: Separate belief from exposure
items.description: Let someone identify as an early believer without requiring them to buy the token.

items.title: Do not bundle an ambiguous promise
items.description: If an NFT is linked to tokens, state exactly what the link means and what it does not mean.

items.title: Publish the supply before minting
items.description: Do not let scarcity appear after the first buyers arrive.

items.title: Reserve a visible creator allocation
items.description: If the creator keeps pieces, publish the number, purpose, and transfer rules.

items.title: Give the collection a transfer test
items.description: Before launch, test minting, metadata, wallet display, transferability, and secondary-sale behavior with a nonvaluable test asset.

items.title: Let holders design one trait
items.description: Give early believers a bounded role in the collection’s visual language.

items.title: Make one artifact together
items.description: Before asking the community for money, have it produce an image, field report, sound, map, or story that could not exist without the group.

items.title: Publish the first-believer list without doxxing anyone
items.description: Use consented handles, pseudonyms, or aggregate counts. Never publish raw wallet identities by default.

items.title: Record the exact chain
items.description: Write down the chain name and verify it from a canonical source.

items.title: Record the exact mint
items.description: A ticker is not an identity. Store the full mint and verify it independently.

items.title: Link the official account
items.description: Use a canonical project account and record when the link was checked.

items.title: Link the creator account
items.description: Record the creator’s public account, but do not infer control of unrelated wallets.

items.title: Record the token name and symbol
items.description: Preserve capitalization and punctuation. Copycats thrive in ambiguity.

items.title: Check for relaunches
items.description: Search whether the name, artwork, or social account existed before this mint.

items.title: Check for impersonators
items.description: Verify every linked site, account, community, and contract against the official source.

items.title: Freeze the identity card
items.description: Publish a one-page identity card with mint, chain, creator, launch time, official links, and known aliases.

items.title: Record the status
items.description: Mark the token pre-migration, migrated, paused, inactive, banned, or unknown.

items.title: Record the timestamp
items.description: Every market observation needs a UTC timestamp. A screenshot without a time is a mood.

items.title: Read the creator’s prior work
items.description: Review earlier launches, not only the current promise.

items.title: Count experiments honestly
items.description: List prior tokens, their stated purpose, their observed peak, and their current status without turning the table into a trophy case.

items.title: Read the failure posts
items.description: A creator who records losses gives you more information than one who only posts wins.

items.title: Separate candor from competence
items.description: Honesty is valuable. It does not prove that the system will work.

items.title: Ask what the creator is optimizing
items.description: Is the goal art, learning, trading, community, a bot, a social experiment, or a revenue stream?

items.title: Ask what the creator will not do
items.description: A boundary is more useful than a slogan.

items.title: Check the correction history
items.description: Does the creator correct wrong claims visibly, or quietly replace them?

items.title: Check the source trail
items.description: Every important claim should point to a transaction, lock, code change, or dated artifact.

items.title: Ask who can operate the project
items.description: If one person disappears, what remains?

items.title: Record conflicts
items.description: If the creator benefits from a behavior they are encouraging, say so plainly.

items.title: Name the bot’s job
items.description: Describe the bot in one sentence without calling it intelligent.

items.title: Publish the inputs
items.description: List the public signals the bot observes.

items.title: Publish the outputs
items.description: Explain whether it buys, sells, alerts, scores, filters, or reports.

items.title: Publish the non-goals
items.description: State what the bot is not designed to detect.

items.title: Publish the known bugs
items.description: A known flaw is a risk boundary, not a confession to hide.

items.title: Separate bot activity from community activity
items.description: Do not call bot volume organic community demand.

items.title: Show one false positive
items.description: A failed call teaches more than a perfect screenshot.

items.title: Show one false negative
items.description: Document a token the bot missed and why.

items.title: Record strategy changes
items.description: Timestamp every meaningful change to entry, exit, filtering, or migration logic.

items.title: Avoid copy-trading language
items.description: The bot’s action is not an instruction to anyone else.

items.title: Publish the bot’s operating window
items.description: Readers need to know whether silence means no signal, no run, or no post.

items.title: Define the bot’s emergency stop
items.description: Explain who can pause it and under what conditions.

items.title: Record total supply
items.description: Verify it from the chain or canonical platform source.

items.title: Check creator allocation
items.description: Find the creator allocation and state what remains unknown.

items.title: Check holder concentration
items.description: Look for clusters, not just the top-holder percentage.

items.title: Check linked wallets carefully
items.description: A wallet relationship is an observation, not proof of common control.

items.title: Check liquidity
items.description: Record liquidity depth and timestamp. Do not confuse market cap with exit capacity.

items.title: Check trading volume
items.description: Separate volume, transaction count, unique traders, and suspected bot activity.

items.title: Check the bonding curve state
items.description: State how far the token is from migration and what threshold applies.

items.title: Explain what migration changes
items.description: Document venue, liquidity, fees, market makers, and new failure modes.

items.title: Check whether migration is automatic
items.description: If it is not, identify the required action and responsible party.

items.title: Check the DEX destination
items.description: Verify the exact venue and pool after migration. Do not trust a screenshot alone.

items.title: Check lock claims
items.description: Record lock amount, beneficiary, duration, and transaction receipt.

items.title: Check unlock dates
items.description: Put them on a calendar visible to the community.

items.title: Check burn claims
items.description: A burn is only meaningful with amount, source wallet, destination, and transaction.

items.title: Check whether burned supply matters
items.description: A percentage can sound large while changing little about holder concentration or liquidity.

items.title: Check creator fees
items.description: Explain who earns fees, when, and what public promise governs them.

items.title: Check whether funds can be returned
items.description: If the community funds infrastructure, define refund conditions before collecting.

items.title: Ask the community to solve a research question
items.description: Choose a question with a public answer instead of a payment target.

items.title: Run a holder-distribution audit
items.description: Let several people reproduce the result independently.

items.title: Run a creator-wallet audit
items.description: Use public addresses only and label uncertain connections.

items.title: Run a bot-behavior audit
items.description: Compare bot activity with non-bot activity over a fixed interval.

items.title: Run a migration rehearsal
items.description: Write the post-migration plan before migration begins.

items.title: Build a community receipt board
items.description: Track completed checks, sources, corrections, and unresolved questions.

items.title: Give contributors credit
items.description: Use consented pseudonyms or roles, not wallet exposure.

items.title: Publish a weekly field note
items.description: Report one thing learned, one thing shipped, one thing wrong, and one next test.

items.title: Publish a public changelog
items.description: Let readers see whether the project changes in response to evidence.

items.title: Create a correction badge
items.description: Make changing one’s mind a visible contribution rather than a humiliation.

items.title: Create a “not yet” badge
items.description: Reward restraint when the evidence is insufficient.

items.title: Make the checklist forkable
items.description: Let other communities reuse it and return improvements.

items.title: Mission: verify the identity card
items.description: The first mission should eliminate ambiguity, not produce hype.

items.title: Mission: find the oldest artifact
items.description: Locate the earliest public evidence of the creator’s stated idea.

items.title: Mission: reproduce one bot result
items.description: Use public inputs and document whether the result matches.

items.title: Mission: identify one falsifier
items.description: Ask what would make the current story wrong.

items.title: Mission: produce the believer collection
items.description: Co-design Print.World traits, metadata, and rules.

items.title: Mission: make the collection survive the token
items.description: Write a cultural description that does not mention price.

items.title: Mission: publish a failure card
items.description: Turn one mistake into a compact public lesson.

items.title: Mission: review the migration plan
items.description: Have a reader find the missing assumption.

items.title: Mission: audit the community funding proposal
items.description: Check destination, target, refund rule, and receipt path.

items.title: Mission: build the post-DEX checklist
items.description: The pre-DEX book should not pretend the risk ends at launch.

items.title: Create one canonical landing page
items.description: Put the identity card, checklist, receipts, collection, and corrections in one place.

items.title: Use one link convention
items.description: Every post should lead to a stable artifact, not a maze of temporary links.

items.title: Publish diagrams before slogans
items.description: A simple flow from launch to migration is more useful than another “moon” image.

items.title: Turn receipts into cards
items.description: Use the same fields every time: claim, source, timestamp, scope, uncertainty.

items.title: Make screenshots readable
items.description: A receipt no one can read is decoration.

items.title: Use threads for mechanisms
items.description: One post should carry one mechanism or one decision.

items.title: Use memes for memory
items.description: A meme can compress a lesson; it cannot replace the receipt.

items.title: Keep the voice human
items.description: The creator’s public uncertainty is an asset. Do not sand it into corporate copy.

items.title: State that participation is optional
items.description: No one should be pressured to buy, contribute, mint, or remain.

items.title: State what the project cannot guarantee
items.description: Name price, liquidity, migration, bot performance, NFT value, and creator availability.

items.title: State what the creator will disclose
items.description: Set a schedule for locks, burns, transfers, bot changes, and corrections.

items.title: State what the community owns
items.description: Define whether members own art, access, governance, receipts, or only their individual assets.

items.title: State what is not being sold
items.description: Do not imply that a membership NFT is an investment contract, a guaranteed exit, or a claim on future work unless that has been legally reviewed.

items.title: Create a quiet exit path
items.description: A holder should be able to leave without being shamed or harassed.

items.title: Create a dispute path
items.description: Name where questions, corrections, and concerns go.

items.title: Preserve the archive
items.description: Keep dated copies of the identity card, claims, receipts, and corrections.

items.title: Ask whether the community has built something together
items.description: If not, the DEX is probably being asked to perform the work of belonging.

items.title: Ask whether the DEX changes the underlying trust conditions
items.description: If it only makes the token visible on a terminal, call it visibility infrastructure—not trust.

items.title: Pay only after the evidence path exists
items.description: The DEX may eventually be useful. It should be the consequence of a community that has identified itself, produced receipts, survived disagreement, and chosen the next experiment together. It should not be the first proof that the project cares.
